output.subject: We've received your concern about your August mortgage payment
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for speaking with us about your mortgage. We understand how stressful a credit report issue can be, especially with an important date coming up, and we appreciate you taking the time to explain your situation.

We want to confirm that we have your complaint. As you told us, a 30-day late payment was reported on your mortgage for August. You mentioned that you made the August payment on 8/23 through online banking and believe it arrived before the due date, so you are disputing the late report and have asked for it to be corrected on your credit report.

You also told us that you are closing on a refinance on 10/3 and that your lender needs a corrected credit report before then. We understand that this date matters a great deal to you.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint, and we will respond within 10 business days. If you have anything you'd like to add in the meantime, such as payment confirmation details or information from your lender, please let us know and we will pass it to the team.

We're sorry for the worry this has caused.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Refinance closing is 10/3; the 10-business-day response may land close to or after that date, so decide whether faster contact is needed.
Rep note says payment history shows the payment was received before the due date; the draft does not state this, so decide whether to confirm it.
Rep submitted a credit bureau correction request; the draft does not mention it, so decide whether to tell the customer and what status to give.
Rep advised the customer the bureau update could take up to 30 days, which may not fit the 10/3 closing; decide whether to address this.
Decide whether to offer a letter for the customer's refinance lender confirming the payment was on time.
Online banking confirmation number and verified SSN were left out of the draft on purpose; keep them out of the reply.
No specific outcome is promised; the analyst must decide on the credit report correction the customer requested.
